critical_code_review_comments: server.py heartbeat builds binance_worker_name with a defensive '<account>.<prefix>.<short>' pattern but iter-11 sets prefix=''; the empty-prefix branch produces '<account>.<short>' which matches the contract — code is correct but would benefit from a unit-style test for the prefix='' code path (covered indirectly by iter-11 heartbeat test).

pool_proxy.MultiPoolManager.register_device only registers on PRIMARY (RVN) class — this is the documented design (a phone cannot mine 11 algos at once) but the public/admin distinction means workers_registered counter on non-primary classes will always be 0; consider surfacing this asymmetry in pow_status_note to avoid 'why is BTC.workers_registered=0?' confusion for new admins.

MultiPoolManager constructor instantiates 11 PoolStatus + PoolConnector at MODULE IMPORT time; if POOL_ENDPOINTS is hot-reloaded the singletons are stale. Acceptable today (endpoints are immutable env-driven), but document the constraint.

routers/pool.py builds public message via _build_public_message; consider adding 'standby' literal (only 'Live'/'Reconnecting'/'Standby' surfaced) — already correct, just worth a doc comment so future devs don't add coin/algo strings to the public branch.

config.py POW_STATUS is a hard-coded module-level string ('native_pow_pending'); when native PoW ships, flipping to 'native_pow_active' will require a code change rather than env var — consider POW_STATUS = os.environ.get('POW_STATUS', 'native_pow_pending') so ops can flip without redeploy.
